trust_decision.summary: Whether a client-supplied ciphertext in a transit-engine decrypt request is long enough, and present at all, to give a 12-byte AES-GCM nonce before slicing and gcm.Open; decided only in ciphertextContainer.UnmarshalJSON and the decrypt handler.

landing_point.why: The summary names ciphertextContainer.UnmarshalJSON and short ciphertexts; the unchecked slice fullCiphertext[:aesGCMNonceSize] is right there.

fix_sites.entry_point: /v1/transit/decrypt/{name}: request struct field becomes a pointer so a missing ciphertext is detectable
/v1/transit/decrypt/{name}: nil check added before key derivation and symmetricDecryptRaw (fix.diff:38-47)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The only other changed site is the missing-field route (zero-value container with a nil nonce reaching gcm.Open, coordinator/internal/transitengineapi/crypto.go:57, via transitengineapi.go:47 and :213). It sits in the same package, one file away, so it is an input-shape variant, not an out-of-scope module.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could argue that a request with no 'ciphertext' field never calls UnmarshalJSON, so it is outside the report's 'short ciphertext' bug; but a zero-value container with an empty nonce still makes gcm.Open panic (crypto.go:57).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Round-trip encrypt then decrypt must keep working, including ciphertexts whose body after the nonce is empty or short (a nonce plus only a GCM tag), and any key version vN. A fix that requires len > nonce+tag, or that rejects the MarshalJSON format, would break valid output from the encrypt route.

O6_input_shapes: decoded ciphertext shorter than 12 bytes (e.g. 'vault:v1:AAAA'), fix.diff:13-15
ciphertext field missing entirely ('{}'), so the container keeps its zero value and the nonce is nil, fix.diff:27-29,38-47
well-formed but unauthenticated ciphertext: now 400 instead of 500, fix.diff:59-60

O7_producer.where: coordinator/internal/transitengineapi/crypto.go:66-88 (UnmarshalJSON, invoked implicitly by json.Decoder in parseRequest, coordinator/internal/transitengineapi/transitengineapi.go:298)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A planted 'rewrap' or batch-decrypt route (OpenBao transit has /rewrap/{name} and batch_input) that parses ciphertextContainer values from a slice or a second field and opens them through its own nonce split.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The package mirrors the OpenBao transit API (transitengineapi.go:107-109), whose rewrap and batch endpoints are natural next features; a maintainer would copy the decrypt handler and might split the nonce inline.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A helper for a different on-disk or legacy ciphertext format (e.g. without the 'vault:' prefix) that slices the nonce from raw bytes without a length check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Legacy or compat parsers are commonly added next to the main format; only a WHERE-type extra, though.

O9_family: improper array index validation / unchecked slice bounds (CWE-129), leading to a per-request handler panic

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.25.6 (go.mod:3); the repo is Nix/just-based, but plain 'go test ./coordinator/internal/transitengineapi/...' should work after the modules are vendored or downloaded
O10_build.project_tests: coordinator/internal/transitengineapi/transitengineapi_test.go (TestTransitAPICyclic, httptest mux with a fake state guard), coordinator/internal/transitengineapi/crypto_test.go

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a length check in UnmarshalJSON only, leaving the missing-field (zero-value container, nil nonce) route that panics in gcm.Open.

out_of_scope_notes: net/http recovers handler panics per request, so the impact is a logged panic and a dropped connection rather than a coordinator crash; the 'dos' flag is weak.
